title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and age-related macular degeneration
subtitle: Evidence map for GLP-1 statements

text_segments.text: Human observational studies present heterogeneous, context-dependent evidence regarding the effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and similar weight-loss drugs on age-related macular degeneration (AMD) (PMID:41683853).

In both diabetic and non-diabetic obese populations, GLP-1 RAs are consistently associated with a significantly reduced risk of developing early, nonexudative (dry) AMD and may slow its progression (PMID:41129133; PMID:40712124; PMID:39863057).
However, evidence regarding exudative (neovascular) AMD is conflicting.

While some studies report a reduced risk or no significant difference in exudative AMD progression (PMID:40712124; PMID:39863057; PMID:41129133; PMID:41453515), one large cohort study found a 2-fold increased risk of incident neovascular AMD in diabetic patients treated with GLP-1 RAs (PMID:40471562).

Consequently, while GLP-1 RAs show promise for early AMD, their long-term ocular safety, particularly concerning neovascular AMD, requires individualized assessment and monitoring (PMID:41857480; PMID:41683853).
